issues.description: The UML in problem_statement.md declares numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as double, but the provided solution (and the intended implementation) uses int for these attributes and for related getters/operations. This mismatch between the specification and the solution/template can confuse students about which data type to implement and about expected return types for methods that use these attributes.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the types consistent. Either update problem_statement.md UML to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int (to match the solution and typical use as counts), or change the solution/template to use double for these attributes and adjust the getter/return types and any arithmetic (including casting for methods declared to return int). Prefer updating the UML to int to avoid unnecessary use of floating-point for counts.
